title: Spring Cloud & Microservices Fundamentals
description: Learn microservices architecture and the Spring Cloud ecosystem at the developer level: why teams split systems into services, how independently deployed services communicate, what distributed-system problems appear, and which Spring Cloud tools address them — preparing for dedicated Eureka Service Discovery and Spring Cloud Gateway trees.

nodes.label: Monoliths, Microservices & Tradeoffs
nodes.description: Distinguish a monolith from a microservices architecture, understand why teams split systems for independent deployment, scaling, and team ownership, and weigh those benefits against the real complexity costs before deciding to split anything.

nodes.label: The Spring Cloud Ecosystem
nodes.description: Distinguish what Spring Boot provides from what Spring Cloud adds, understand Spring Cloud as a collection of projects solving different distributed-system problems rather than a single library, and maintain Spring Boot/Spring Cloud version compatibility discipline.

nodes.label: Service Boundaries
nodes.description: Design service boundaries around cohesive business capabilities with loose coupling and explicit contracts, and recognize bad boundaries such as the distributed monolith, excessive chattiness, and services that expose their internal tables or classes.

nodes.label: Synchronous Service-to-Service Communication
nodes.description: Implement request/response calls between services with a modern Spring HTTP client, model the expected remote response with a dedicated DTO rather than a shared entity class, and understand how contract changes can break the consuming service.

nodes.label: Remote Failure, Timeouts & Cascading Failure
nodes.description: Recognize that a remote call can fail for reasons a local call never would, design deliberate timeout behavior instead of waiting forever, understand the danger of blind retries under overload, grasp the circuit breaker pattern conceptually, and trace how one slow dependency can cascade failure upstream through a chain.

nodes.description: Experience why hardcoded service locations break down once instances scale, move, or fail, understand the service registry pattern that Eureka will implement, and recognize why an API gateway becomes necessary once clients must reach many backend services.

nodes.description: Manage configuration that multiplies across many services with environment variables, understand the centralized-configuration pattern behind Spring Cloud Config, and keep secrets like credentials and API keys separate from ordinary configuration and out of source control.

nodes.description: Apply the database-per-service ownership principle, recognize how a shared database tightly couples supposedly independent services, and understand why distributed transactions are hard and why some architectures accept eventual consistency instead.
